extended:
**KNOT CABLING AND THE DEGREE OF THE COLORED JONES POLYNOMIAL**

*EFSTRATIA KALFAGIANNI AND ANH T. TRAN*

31 pp, 21 sections.

**Abstract.** We study the behavior of the degree of the colored Jones polynomial and the boundary slopes of knots under the operation of cabling. We show that, under certain hypothesis on this degree, if a knot K satisﬁes the Slope Conjecture then a (p, q)-cable of K satisﬁes the conjecture, provided that p/q is not a Jones slope of K. As an application we prove the Slope Conjecture for iterated cables of adequate knots and for iterated torus knots. Furthermore we show that, for these knots, the degree of the colored Jones polynomial also determines the topology of a surface that satisﬁes the Slope Conjecture.

**Outline.** Front matter; 1.1 The Slope Conjecture; 1 Introduction; 1.2 Cable knots; 1.3 Organization.; 2 Boundary Slopes of Cable Knots; 2.1 Preliminaries and statement of main result; 2.2 Boundary slopes and homology of cable spac; 3 Cables of Knots with period at most two; 3.1 The colored Jones polynomial; 3.2 Cables of knots of period at most 2; 3.3 Strong Slope Conjecture for iterated cable; 3.5 Low crossing knots with period two; 4 Cabling knots with constant a(n); 5 Conjectures; 5.1 Non-alternating Montesinos knots up to nin; 5.2 A family of pretzel knots; 6 Two-fusion knots
